degree: M.DM. in Disaster Management The International Program

sections.name: Mandatory Electives
sections.note:
By default, all students are enrolled in the Regular track (without a thesis). Students interested in the thesis track can apply only at the end of the first semester.
Course description page: https://emergexint.tau.ac.il/course_description

sections.name: General Electives
sections.note:
The program requires students to study 4 credits of general electives. The following options for these credits are:
1. The internship course, which is a year-round course and provides the entire 4 credits.
2. Selection of courses studied in English (or Hebrew if applicable) from the school, faculty, or campus-wide, as long as they meet the following criteria: The relevant students' secretariat of the department where the course is being taught approves enrollment of external students
The course is accredited for a Master's degree
The course has a final exam with an actual score (courses whose final grade is "pass"/"no pass" are not eligble)
The course' exam date does not overlap with other exam dates in the program
3. Courses taught entirely online or courses without mandatory attendance or courses with hybrid teaching that allows students to take the course without physically attending it may also apply if they meet the abovementioned criteria.
4. Enrolling in additional courses from the M.DM. mandatory elective courses list.

sections.name: Final Project
sections.note: The final project is the final paper in the regular track (without thesis). The purpose of the final project is to allow students to experiment and exercise with research tools acquired during their studies. The project will be done by the student in supervision of one of the academic staff members of the School of Public Health, the Sackler Faculty or the School of Management at TAU. High ranking officials in the ministry of health, defense, other governmental agencies, local authorities, emergency services, etc. can also serve as supervisors, even if they are not listed among TAU's academic staff.The final grade for the regular (project) track will comprise of 75% course grading and 25% final project paper (broken down to 10% score by supervisor and 15% score by external judgment).
